clue.text: Warning given to man in the crew's quarters

parts.note: golfers shout fore as a warning to anyone in the ball's path
a castle (rook) is one of the men in chess

explanation.surface: A sailor gets a warning down below decks where the crew sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' simply joins the two pieces. 'Man' is not a person but a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The forward part of a ship below deck is traditionally where the sailors live, so it names their quarters.

clue.text: Bazaar deprived of vitality when openers have left

indicators.note: openers are the opening letters; their leaving means the first two are removed

parts.note: effete means worn out, lacking vitality

explanation.surface: A lifeless charity sale once the opening speakers had gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'openers' sounds like the people who open a fete; it means the first letters, here EF.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fund-raising event with stalls, much like a bazaar.

clue.text: It's inclined to act in a threatening manner

definitions.text: to act in a threatening manner
definitions.meaning: to rear up or storm about menacingly, as a lion rampant

explanation.surface: Someone tends to behave menacingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is a sloping surface, and to ramp is an old verb for rearing up threateningly.

clue.text: Balanchine took steps to express it in writing

definitions.text: Balanchine took steps to express it in writing

parts.words: Balanchine took steps to express it in writing
parts.note: George Balanchine designed ballets; the word for his art means, by its Greek roots, dance writing

explanation.surface: A famous ballet-maker set about putting his ideas down on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: George Balanchine was a celebrated choreographer; 'took steps' means both acted and arranged dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of composing dances, from Greek words for dance and writing.

clue.text: Part of a letter — one pocketed by a slave

indicators.note: the slave holds the numeral inside, as if putting it in a pocket

parts.note: a serf was a bonded labourer, like a slave
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Part of a letter is about a slave pocketing something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' suggests correspondence, but it is a printed character.
explanation.definitionFit: A small finishing stroke on the end of a printed character's stroke is part of the letter.

clue.text: Conspicuous buildings with minarets at the top, surrounded by birds

indicators.note: the larks enclose the other pieces, so they go inside

parts.note: larks are songbirds
and can mean with, together with

indicators.note: the top of a word written downward is its first letter

explanation.surface: Notable towers with minarets are encircled by birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Prominent features or buildings that stand out and help people find their way.

clue.text: A singular rival in the field

indicators.note: making the plural name singular drops its final plural-looking letter

parts.note: Bob Acres is one of the suitors in Sheridan's comedy The Rivals

explanation.surface: A lone competitor stands out on the sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The rival is Bob Acres from Sheridan's 18th-century play The Rivals; put 'singular', the name loses its S.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional unit of land area, roughly the size of a large field, so farmland is reckoned in them.

clue.text: Cook sold fancy southern sweetmeat

indicators.note: to cook something is to fiddle or alter it, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A cook sold a fancy confection from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' reads as a person who made the sweet; it is the instruction to rearrange SOLD FANCY.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun sugar on a stick is a fairground confection, a sweet.

clue.text: Frantically made one try correcting errors

indicators.note: done in a wild frenzy, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone made one more desperate attempt to fix mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Emendatory means serving to emend, to remove faults from a text.

clue.text: Instrument a doctor required during trip in east

indicators.note: the doctor and article sit within the journey word, so during marks a container here

parts.note: a tour is a trip
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medic is needed on a journey through the East to look after a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hand drum with jingles round the rim is a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Formerly part of the region Cerberus guarded

indicators.note: a part of the words is taken, so the letters lie within region Cerberus

explanation.surface: In the old days, the underworld was a region watched over by the dog Cerberus.
explanation.walkthrough: Cerberus is the three-headed dog of Greek myth that guarded Hades.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean at some time in the past.

clue.text: Fellow's attitude about student — one kissed in Ireland

indicators.note: the fellow's name goes around the student letter

parts.note: Barney is a man's name, standing for any fellow
L is a learner, as on L-plates
tone means attitude or manner

explanation.surface: A man's manner towards a student, a person kissed in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The stone at Blarney Castle in County Cork is kissed by visitors for the gift of persuasive talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Visitors to a castle in County Cork kiss this famous rock to gain eloquence.

clue.text: Society mischief-maker used to be freelance

parts.note: an elf is a mischievous sprite in folklore
employed means used, put to use

explanation.surface: A troublemaking member of society once worked on his own account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is a link; 'used to be' reads as a past habit but splits into a synonym and a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone freelance works for themselves rather than an employer.

clue.text: Understanding church skill in deception requires the black art

parts.note: wit means intelligence or understanding
craft means cunning, skill at deceiving

explanation.surface: Grasping church guile calls for black magic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requires' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery, the use of magic, is called the black art.

clue.text: Gymnastic equipment 2 carried in to field

indicators.note: the answer to clue 2 is carried inside the little word

parts.note: refers to the answer to 2 down, a slope
a line is a field of work, as in line of business

explanation.surface: Gym apparatus is carried onto the sports field.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' points to the answer to 2 Down, RAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A taut sprung mat for bouncing is used in gymnastics.

clue.text: Improper to be partisan

definitions.meaning: not according to rule or proper form
a partisan is a guerrilla fighter, a soldier outside the regular army

explanation.surface: Taking sides is not proper behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregular means against the rules, and as a noun names a fighter not in a regular force, like a partisan.

clue.text: It attracts a number to Tyneside, bearing literary works

indicators.note: the outer pieces bear, so carry within, the literary works

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written
Tyneside is in the north-east of England, abbreviated NE
odes are lyrical poems

explanation.surface: Something draws a crowd to Tyneside, carrying books.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturally magnetic rock attracts iron.

clue.text: Widow caught out and fired again

indicators.note: the cricket letter is put out of the word for widow

parts.note: relict is an old word for a widow
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A widow was caught and then dismissed once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire or pipe lit a second time has been rekindled.

clue.text: Fellow scholar catches male butterfly

parts.note: co- is the prefix meaning fellow, as in co-worker

indicators.note: the scholar holds the male letter inside, as one catches something

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, a graduate scholar

explanation.surface: A fellow academic nets a male butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: A common European butterfly takes its name from the punctuation-mark-shaped white spot under its wing.

clue.text: Drug dealer with a load of money in the bank?

definitions.meaning: one who hands out medicines, a pharmacist

definitions.text: with a load of money in the bank?
definitions.meaning: a cash machine is loaded with money in a bank wall

explanation.surface: A drug dealer has made a fortune and banked it.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a cash dispenser, a machine stocked with banknotes at a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist dispenses medicines, and a cash machine dispenses money.

clue.text: An affectedly fashionable person represented her school set

indicators.note: the letters are presented again in a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion-conscious girl stands for her school's set.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dresses showily, as if their only use is to display clothes, is called this.

clue.text: Blatant surrender of river in 1812, say

indicators.note: the piece gives up, so loses, the river

parts.note: Tchaikovsky's 1812 is an overture
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: An obvious capitulation at a river in 1812, the year of Napoleon's retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: '1812' suggests a battle, but it is Tchaikovsky's 1812 Overture.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, not hidden, so blatant.

clue.text: Butcher mostly used old unit of weight

indicators.note: mostly means not all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: to butcher is to kill

explanation.surface: A butcher used an outdated measure of weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for kilogram, a metric measure of mass.

clue.text: Turn up with a note for the brute!

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is written bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Show up with a message for the bully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' reads as arrive; 'Turn' gives GO and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A monster of folklore, a cruel brute.

clue.text: A small number backing the alliance

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the small number is read in reverse

parts.note: six is a small number

explanation.surface: A small number of people support the alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Axis was the alliance of Germany, Italy and Japan in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The Second World War pact of Germany, Italy and Japan was known as this.

clue.text: Alien turns tail, grabbing fellow in anticipation of trouble

indicators.note: the altered alien word grabs, so holds inside, the fellow
the tail end of the alien word is turned about, its last two letters changing places

parts.note: foreign means alien
the letter moved to the very end when the tail is turned
bod is slang for a person, a fellow

explanation.surface: An alien flees, seizing a man, with a sense of looming disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alien' and 'fellow' look like characters in a sci-fi story; the alien becomes FOREING once its tail turns, and 'grabbing' wraps that round the fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreboding is a feeling that something bad is coming, an anticipation of trouble.

clue.text: Pelt an assembly of hunters rejected

indicators.note: rejected suggests thrown back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a meet is a gathering of huntsmen and hounds

explanation.surface: Pelt a gathering of huntsmen who have been turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like throwing things or an animal skin; here it is a verb for rain coming down hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to rain very heavily.

clue.text: Copper reported by a certain number to be plucky

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word for copper is heard rather than seen

parts.note: copper is a metal
some means a certain unspecified number

explanation.surface: A policeman reported by several people is said to be brave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone full of spirit and courage is brave, or plucky.
